title: NostalgiaForInfinity — multi-pair 5m Freqtrade strategy
economic_hypothesis: no stable metric is published; the authoring community reports the strategy as live-traded, which is a claim rather than a measurable original result
assets: the README recommends 40-80 user-selected pairs; the strategy declares no universe
timeframe: 5m — the README says the timeframe must not be overridden
entry_rules: code exists and is versioned, but the file was not read here
risk_rules: 'between 6 and 12 open trades, with unlimited stake' is a range, not a rule; none declared (24/7 market)
parameters: the repository ships an auto-updater; parameters must be pinned to a release tag before they are fixed
claimed_period: the README points at backtest results in per-commit comments
external_results: the repository's own description: rules live in code, results in commit comments
counter_evidence: the README's own recommendations leave the universe and the number of open trades to the user
results are published as commit comments, so the 'original result' is not a stable artifact
the bundled auto-updater (nfi-updater) keeps changing the strategy, which breaks any frozen replication
a 5m strategy with a long tail (-stoploss in config) faces the project's 23.791 bps round trip on every round turn
the project's admission cost is a 23.791 bps round trip, and the source declares no cost model (not stated)
found in the RFC-035S2 strategy-first search; no local backtest influenced this record
